answer: Make every identity earn its place by solving a verifiable delay function before it can act. First, a new agent runs a sequential puzzle taking ten minutes on one CPU core, with no parallel shortcut. Second, the proof is checked instantly and must be redone every epoch. Third, fakes expire when the proof lapses. Running 10,000 clones needs about 280 cores nonstop, roughly $4,000 a month in cloud rent, while one honest agent spends ten idle minutes. Like a lotus opening only at dawn, trust keeps its own clock; a canyon is not dug in a day, and a plume of smoke cannot fake a river's course.
